What happens if one of them do something like break a leg, no work and their jobs are not known for having health insurance. I also notice this is a list of all southern locations nobody listed is trying it in an area where winter or severe weather is a huge issue.

I've always been attracted by this kind of lifestyle, the tinyhouse movement, etc. and I have a couple of thoughts about it. For one, I think it makes a huge difference if you've already 'won' the rat race and now you're looking for something else as opposed to someone who's never been to the mountain top. If you have a financial cushion to fall back on then choosing austerity doesn't feel like poverty. It's a mindset.

Also, while some people are natural loners, to me this would be lonely without a partner, and it would surely test the limits of a relationship to be together so much in this kind of life. I think it would either be the most intense bonding you ever experience with another person or you would wind up not being able to stand each other.

The being online aspect of this story is almost incidental. The internet is a utility like water or electricity.. use as much or as little as you need.
